approved_findings: The only substantive payment-method table delta is a row label and destination change from Crypto in the old capture at line 146 to Stablecoins in the new capture at line 143. Both rows mark Payment Element and Connect Payment Element support in this A/B-test table. This does not establish general stablecoin payment availability, any account's eligibility, or a production experiment outcome; preserve the old row as dated history.

Both captured tables have 34 listed payment-method rows, not the 35 claimed by current source line 21, wiki/concepts/stripe-ab-testing-payment-methods.md lines 63-69, and Stripe index line 438. Queue a bounded correction to the row count and qualify it as the dated table, not a timeless universal support count. The nine Connect-unsupported rows named by source line 21 persist; the Connect footnote explains that off-Stripe eligibility steps cannot be completed by platforms for connected accounts (new line 165, old line 168).

Current source line 18 and concept line 31 compress Stripe's illustrative sample calculation into a general 80,000-session rule. Both captures say 50% is a recommendation, not an enforced default, and 80,000 is the example for an even split, 100 basis point conversion difference, and 5% significance level (new line 30; old line 30). The page's methodology uses a dynamic power calculation at 80% power for a 1% difference (new line 111; old line 113). Preserve allocation, effect-size, statistical threshold, and power assumptions; actual required sessions vary.

Concept line 40 equates gray indicators with fewer than 80% of required sessions, while both captures state that green or yellow differences display once at least 80% of the estimated sessions are reached and gray means insufficient sessions to reliably determine significance (new lines 70-76; old lines 72-78). Do not infer that every experiment at or above 80% receives a significant green/yellow badge or that a result is proven causal.

The page remains scoped to dynamic payment methods with Payment Element Web plus Payment Intents API or Checkout in payment mode (new lines 19,119-125). Dashboard-only start, stop and management, one experiment per configuration, pausing, 180-day end, eligible-session filters, and Connect platform-versus-connected-account boundaries persist. Other diff changes are buyer-to-customer wording, image URL rendering, numbering, and table formatting.
approved_conflicts: Source line 21, concept lines 63-69, and Stripe index line 438 say 35 supported payment methods, but old raw lines 133-166 and new raw lines 130-163 each contain 34 method rows.

Source line 18 and concept line 31 present the 80,000-session example without the full even-split, target-effect, significance, and dynamic power assumptions at old raw lines 30,113 and new raw lines 30,111.

Concept line 40 treats gray as strictly below 80% of required sessions, which the old and new indicator guidance does not state; at least 80% is a display threshold for green/yellow difference, not a guaranteed significance result.
Source and concept omit the dated Crypto-to-Stablecoins row wording change; do not broaden that table label into a claim that the merchant's account has stablecoin access.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the old Crypto row as 2026-05-08 captured evidence rather than claiming it was deprecated or universally replaced for all accounts.

Retain the no-code Dashboard experiment-management boundary, required dynamic payment methods and integration modes, sample assumptions, eligible-session denominator, and Connect platform-only authority.
Preserve original local CDN asset references as historical source metadata; newer remote image URLs are presentational and are not evidence of tested functionality.
unresolved_questions: Neither capture verifies a specific merchant's dynamic-payment-method configuration, eligibility for a table-listed method, Connect account activation, or ability to run a particular experiment.
The page documents statistical methodology and illustrative power calculations, but no observed sample, result, revenue lift, or causal business outcome was produced or independently verified here.
